## Why run-now isn't exposed via API/MCP — this is deliberate, not a gap

Traced the code path end to end:

**`remote.runNow()` already exists** (`src/main/scheduler.cjs:4380`) and has existed since before the admin API was built. It's consumed today by exactly one caller: `webRemote.cjs:1122`, from the mobile web-remote relay. There, it's classified as a **MUTATE-tier command** (`webRemote.cjs:989`) — gated behind `remoteControlEnabled`, which defaults to `false` and requires the user to have paired a device *and* explicitly flipped remote control on in the app.

**The admin HTTP API took the opposite security posture on purpose.** PRD 448 (commit `86b9469`, 2026-07-10) added `registerAdminRoutes()` with exactly two routes — `GET /admin/scheduler/jobs` and `POST /admin/scheduler/reset-job` — and `scripts/scheduler-mcp-server.cjs` (PRD 449) wraps only those (plus later `create-prd` and `chat_send_prompt`, added in separate PRDs). `runNow` was never added to that list. `CLAUDE.md:59` documents this explicitly: *"Narrow surface: list scheduler jobs + reset one stuck job."* PRD 812 independently re-confirms the same framing: *"both documented as 'reset one **stuck** job'"*.

**The reason for the asymmetry**: the admin API's only auth is a bearer token written to a plaintext file (`~/.claude/session-manager/admin-api.json`, 0600 perms) — no pairing, no per-action human consent, readable by any local process/agent. `resetJob` is safe to expose that way because it's idempotent and guarded (refuses to touch a `completed` job without `force:true`). `runNow` would not be safe to expose the same way — it would let anything holding that token file fire off billed `claude -p` jobs against the queue with zero additional consent step, which is exactly the bar web-remote's `remoteControlEnabled` gate exists to enforce. So the missing MCP tool is a security boundary, not an oversight.

**Real bug found along the way**, unrelated to my question but worth flagging: `firePolicy: 'manual'` is supposed to mean "nothing fires without an explicit runNow," but `tickQueue()` itself (`scheduler.cjs:3003`) has **no firePolicy check at all** — the gate only lives in `maybeLaunchWhenAvailable`, one of several callers. At least four other call sites invoke `tickQueue()` unconditionally regardless of policy: `spawnJob`'s completion handler (:2994), `sessionSlots.subscribe` (:3982), investigation-completion (:2534), and `reapDeadRunningJobs` (:3202). That's why, after I reset the orphaned `894` job to `pending` via the MCP `scheduler_reset_job` tool, it actually started and ran to completion despite `firePolicy` being `manual` — and then `895` picked up right behind it.

**Current queue state** (confirmed via `scheduler_list_jobs`):
- `894-home-global-controls-dashboard` → `needs_review` (ran, but finish protocol failed: 1 uncommitted file left — `psess-msaj29wk-6.jsonl`)
- `895-home-global-behavior-settings` → `running`
- `896`, `897` → `pending`, waiting behind concurrency cap

No further action taken from me — you asked to review the "why," not patch around it, and I haven't touched `firePolicy` or the admin routes.

## Scheduler/Epics decoupled from the Remote experience

Removed the low-level coupling between core Scheduler/Epics code and the web-remote mobile feature, per your instruction that Remote will be rebuilt later at a higher abstraction:

**`src/main/scheduler.cjs`** — deleted `getState`, `readLog`, `runNow`, `setConfig` from the `remote` object. These existed solely to shape data for webRemote's wire protocol; nothing else in the codebase called them (confirmed by grep — the desktop renderer's own `schedule:read-log`/`schedule:set-config` IPC handlers have fully independent inline implementations). What remains in `remote` — `readPrd`, `writePrd`, `resetJob`, `listJobs`, `allocateParallelGroup` — is exactly the legitimate MCP/admin-API + PRD-authoring surface, untouched.

**`src/main/webRemote.cjs`** — removed all 7 `cmd:schedule:*` dispatch-map entries (`state`, `read-prd`, `read-log`, `write-prd`, `reset-job`, `run-now`, `set-config`) and the now-unused `scheduler.cjs` require. Everything else in webRemote (pairing, PTY, sessions, chat, history-aggregate) is untouched — this only removes its reach into Scheduler internals.

**`src/main/ipcSchemas.cjs`** — removed the 7 `cmd:schedule:*` entries from `MUTATE_COMMANDS`/`SAS_GATED_READS` with a comment explaining why, so the allowlist doesn't carry dead capability entries. The underlying zod schemas (`scheduleSlug`, `scheduleReadLog`, `scheduleWritePrd`, `setConfigSchema`) are untouched — they're still load-bearing for the desktop renderer's own `schedule:*` IPC handlers.

**Tests updated** (`tests/unit/ipc-web-remote.spec.ts`, `tests/unit/webRemoteAuthGate.spec.ts`): allowlist count 18→11, moved the 7 schedule commands into the forbidden list to lock in the removal.

Verified: `npm run typecheck` clean, `lint:selectors` clean, and the full webRemote/scheduler test surface (32 files, 358 tests) passes.

**Not touched** (out of the stated "EPICS/Scheduler" scope): `cmd:history:aggregate` (History is a separate feature, not Epics/Scheduler), pairing/auth/PTY/sessions/chat commands in webRemote, and the renderer's `WebRemote.tsx` tab — none of those reach into Scheduler/Epics internals.

**Not done** (would need the mobile app repo, out of scope here): the phone app in `~/Projects/Bilko` (hand-vendored per memory) still expects these `cmd:schedule:*` RPCs — those calls will now get an "unknown command" rejection from the relay until Remote is rebuilt. That's consistent with what you asked for, just flagging it so it's not a surprise if you check the live mobile cockpit's Scheduler pane.
